subject.title: [Bug]: Isolated cron runs fall through to wildcard toolsBySender and lose trusted group tools

question: Should an isolated cron job delivered to a configured trusted group receive a dedicated internal tool-policy identity, and if so which persisted cron/delivery facts are sufficient to authorize it without inheriting any external sender authority?
rationale: The report identifies a loss of intended authority, but assigning elevated tools to a senderless scheduled run changes the authorization boundary and cannot be resolved safely from local inference alone.

options.title: Define a narrow cron-internal policy
options.body: Authorize only an explicit, persisted trusted cron/delivery contract and retain all other current tool-policy intersections.

options.title: Keep cron senderless by default
options.body: Retain wildcard sender policy for isolated cron runs and document the dedicated-agent configuration workaround.

options.title: Generalize delegated lineage
options.body: Extend requester-policy inheritance only if maintainers establish that cron runs have a legitimate authority-bearing parent projection.

recommendation.title: Define a narrow cron-internal policy
recommendation.body: Authorize only an explicit, persisted trusted cron/delivery contract and retain all other current tool-policy intersections.

likelyOwner.reason: Their adjacent delegated-run work is the closest available history signal for the sender-policy authorization boundary.
